correctness.rationale: For prime powers the exact identity is \(G(p^e)=(e-1)p^{e-1}\). For two-prime support, direct expansion gives \(G(p^a q^b)=p^{a-1}q^{b-1}((a-1)q+(b-1)p+1)\), making the threshold \(8\) and equality case \(12\) immediate. For squarefree numbers, \(G(qm)=qG(m)+(m-\varphi(m))\), while a squarefree triple has \(G(pqr)=p+q+r-1\), whose minimum is \(9\) uniquely at \(30\). The radical identity shows repeated exponents can only increase the three-prime case. The packaged verifier independently confirms all stated fibers and support inequalities through \(10^6\).

value.rationale: A344178 already singles out its first two fibers, so the next exact fibers are a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The result is strengthened beyond isolated values by sharp structural thresholds according to prime support: \(2\) for composite prime powers, \(8\) for nonsquarefree two-prime support, and \(9\) for at least three distinct primes, each with a unique equality case. This explains the initial gaps of the sequence and completely resolves every value through the first three-prime threshold.
